blocks.text: Domain adaptive pretraining, DAPT, is a specific application of the continued pretraining technique covered in the previous topic, deliberately scoped to a well defined domain corpus, biomedical literature, legal documents, financial filings, rather than continued pretraining broad general goal.

This topic covers what distinguishes DAPT as a named, well studied variant, how to choose a genuinely relevant domain corpus, and how it commonly combines with the task adaptive pretraining covered in the next topic.
1. What DAPT Is
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472911950-731363458.png

DAPT further pretrains a general model on a large corpus of text specifically drawn from one target domain, using the same self-supervised next-token objective covered in the previous Continued Pretraining topic, deepening the model familiarity with that domain vocabulary and content patterns.
2. DAPT as a Named Variant of Continued Pretraining

blocks.alt: DAPT as a Named Variant of Continued Pretraining
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472911950-176610150.png

Continued pretraining, covered in the previous topic, is the general umbrella term, DAPT specifically refers to the well studied case where the corpus is drawn from one clearly defined domain, this specificity is what makes DAPT a distinctly named and separately researched technique rather than a redundant restatement of the same idea.
3. Choosing a Domain Corpus
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472911950-818734441.png

DAPT corpus choice directly determines what domain familiarity the model gains, biomedical papers for a medical assistant, legal filings for a legal tool, financial reports for a finance application, the corpus needs to genuinely represent the vocabulary and content style the eventual downstream task will involve.

blocks.text: 4. Checking Corpus Relevance Before Committing
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472911951-598092365.png

Before investing in DAPT, it is worth explicitly checking that the chosen corpus is genuinely relevant to the downstream task, a broad, loosely related corpus produces weaker domain adaptation benefit than a tightly relevant one, this relevance check is a cheap step that avoids wasting significant compute on a poorly targeted corpus.

blocks.title: Corpus relevance matters more than corpus size alone
blocks.content: Research studying DAPT has found that a smaller, highly relevant domain corpus often outperforms a larger but more loosely related one, quality and genuine relevance of the corpus matters as much as its raw size.

blocks.text: 5. Combining DAPT With TAPT
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472912491-622150283.png

DAPT is commonly followed by task adaptive pretraining, TAPT, covered in the next topic, narrowing further from a broad domain corpus to a corpus matching the specific downstream task even more closely, this two-stage combination, DAPT then TAPT, has shown particularly strong results in published research.
6. Measuring Whether DAPT Was Worth It

blocks.alt: Measuring Whether DAPT Was Worth It
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472912493-575304220.png

Since DAPT adds meaningful compute cost, connecting to the cost optimization considerations covered in an earlier topic, evaluating its actual benefit, comparing downstream task performance with and without the DAPT stage, confirms whether the investment paid off for a specific domain and task rather than assuming it automatically will.
7. Addressing Vocabulary Gaps
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472912493-30845886.png

A common motivation for DAPT is a genuine vocabulary gap, specialized domain terminology, abbreviations, and phrasing conventions that a general pretraining corpus rarely covers deeply, DAPT specifically targets closing this gap by exposing the model to substantial in-domain text.
8. DAPT in the Broader Fine-Tuning Pipeline

Like continued pretraining generally, covered in the previous topic, DAPT happens before supervised fine-tuning and alignment stages, covered throughout this course, establishing domain familiarity as a foundation the later, more targeted training stages build on.
9. When DAPT Is Worth the Investment

DAPT tends to be worth its added cost specifically when a domain has genuinely distinctive vocabulary or content patterns a general model lacks, and when a sufficiently large, relevant domain corpus is actually available, for domains that overlap heavily with general pretraining data already, the benefit is likely to be smaller.
Worked Example

A team building a biomedical research assistant runs DAPT on a large corpus of biomedical research papers before their supervised fine-tuning stage, checking beforehand that the corpus genuinely matches the kind of biomedical content their downstream task will involve.

Comparing downstream evaluation performance with and without the DAPT stage confirms a measurable improvement specifically on biomedical terminology handling, validating that the added compute cost was worthwhile for their specific domain, they then proceed to a TAPT stage, covered in the next topic, narrowing further toward their specific task before final supervised fine-tuning.
Common Mistakes

items: Choosing a domain corpus that is only loosely related to the actual downstream task, weakening the adaptation benefit
Skipping a relevance check on the domain corpus before investing significant compute in DAPT
Not measuring whether DAPT actually improved downstream performance, assuming the benefit rather than confirming it
Applying DAPT to a domain that already overlaps heavily with general pretraining data, where the added benefit is minimal

blocks.text: Practice

For a specialized domain and downstream task you are familiar with, identify a specific corpus you would use for DAPT, and explain how you would check its relevance before committing compute, and what evaluation comparison would confirm whether the DAPT stage was actually worthwhile.
Key Takeaway

Domain adaptive pretraining is a well studied, specifically scoped application of continued pretraining that targets one well defined domain corpus, closing vocabulary and content gaps a general model has, and it commonly combines with the task adaptive pretraining covered in the next topic for even stronger downstream results, though its benefit should be measured rather than assumed given its meaningful added compute cost.
